answer: The falcon multiplier is published, charged in comet, and ledge lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 769 identities would post 4664 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
